newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita leads lively Helsinki broadly higher.
newsitem.headline: Merita leads lively Helsinki broadly higher.

text.p: Bank shares took the HEX index to a new 12-month high close on Tuesday after lively trade sparked by a rally in Merita as foreign selling pressures on the share eased.
The HEX index rose 0.56 percent to 2,186.24. Volume was a hefty 470 million markka.
Brokers saw scope for more gains on Wednesday as the strong mood was reinforced by slightly softer than expected U.S. purchasing manager index (NAPM) data.
"Shares could continue to rally as there was strong demand at the end of the session," one broker said.
Banking group Merita's A share closed active trade 0.63 markka up at 10.60. OKO tracked Merita, adding 0.50 markka to close at 43.50. Alandsbanken rose 0.70 markka to 81.70.
Insurance shares also extended gains after last weeks' talk of possible restructuring of the sector's ownership. Sampo closed lively trade at a new two-year high 344.00, up 14.00.
Forestries advanced in active trade as bargain-hunters showed up after recent losses.
Metal industry shares were boosted by optimistic comments from industry executives and by paper machine group Valmet's report of healthy January-August profit.
Steel group Rautaruukki closed active trade at a new calendar year-high 41.20, up 1.20. Valmet added 1.00 markka to 76.30.
But telecoms group Nokia fell 2.40 markka to 201.50. Trade in the share accounted for just over a fifth of total bourse volume.
Cargo shipping company Finnlines closed 1.00 markka lower at 97.00. Trade was active and was boosted by some big in-house deals, but brokers could not explain the activity in the share.
